currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 was described as a year of capacity and capability expansion. The Company operates a growing manufacturing footprint across Maharashtra and Karnataka, with continued development of its facility at Mahad, Raigad and a new facility at Bengaluru strengthening its production capabilities. During the year the Company also progressed a captive solar power initiative and established an in-house design and manufacturing capability in the advanced defence and aerospace segment, extending its composite-fabrication expertise into the design, engineering and manufacture of unmanned aerial vehicles; this was further broadened through a dedicated joint venture, Jyoti Aeronext Private Limited, offering drone-enabled services for civilian and commercial applications, positioning the Company across both drone products and drone-based services. Funding capacity was strengthened by the Initial Public Offering completed during the year and the listing of equity shares on the NSE EMERGE platform on 11 August 2025, with the Board stating that the resulting increase in net worth provides a foundation to support future growth and expansion plans; no dividend was recommended so as to conserve resources for growth plans and business expansion. No commissioning dates, project cost or added capacity figures for the Mahad, Bengaluru or solar initiatives are stated in this text.

risks.note: HDPE/PP granule prices are linked to crude oil and subject to volatility; mitigated through inventory management, supplier diversification and procurement planning.

A significant share of revenue remains concentrated in the traditional carboy/barrel product lines; mitigated through active diversification into pail buckets, toys, automotive components and the new defence/aerospace drone vertical.

risks.risk: Execution risk in aerospace and defence
risks.note: Certification, airworthiness and defence-procurement cycles are inherently long and determined by external agencies, which can influence the pace at which specific engagements translate into scaled, recurring revenue; mitigated through in-house design, manufacturing and testing capability, a diversified product-and-service pipeline and sustained engagement with defence R&D organisations, the armed forces and other institutional customers.

risks.risk: Operational risk — product quality and skilled manpower
risks.note: Maintaining consistent product quality in mass production and availability of skilled manpower remain ongoing operational challenges; mitigated through inventory management techniques, process controls and retention-focused HR practices.

risks.risk: Competition risk and end-market demand fluctuation
risks.note: The Company operates in a competitive environment exposed to demand fluctuations across packaging, infrastructure, automotive and FMCG end-markets; mitigated through product and end-market diversification.

risks.risk: Industry fragmentation and supplier-side concentration in the value chain
risks.note: Polymer feedstock (HDPE, PP) is supplied by a small number of large integrated petrochemical producers, while the downstream processing and moulding segment in which JGPL operates is highly fragmented and dominated by small and medium enterprises, competing principally on quality, customisation, delivery reliability and proximity to the customer's plant.

risks.risk: Plastic-waste regulation and Extended Producer Responsibility obligations
risks.note: EPR rules under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016 as amended are progressively pushing the industry toward recycled-content and reuse obligations, administered through the CPCB's centralised EPR portal.

risks.risk: Pace of commercialisation of the new drone and aerospace vertical
risks.note: The cautionary statement identifies the pace of commercialisation of the Company's new drone and aerospace vertical among the external and internal factors beyond its control that could cause actual results to differ materially from forward-looking statements.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's sustained expansion in industrial activity and private consumption (real GDP estimated to have grown 7.7% in FY 2025-26) provides a supportive demand environment for the existing blow moulded plastics business
- Core packaging demand remains anchored in the chemical, lubricant and industrial oil, pharmaceutical, paint, adhesive and food and agro industries, where organised buyers increasingly favour quality-assured, customised suppliers over unorganised players
- Policy-backed tailwind in defence and aerospace — Atmanirbhar Bharat capital allocation, a widening PLI footprint and a policy preference for domestically designed and manufactured unmanned systems over imports
- Liberalised Drone Rules, 2021 (forms reduced from 25 to 5, fee types from 72 to 4), a PLI scheme for drones and drone components with an approved outlay of Rs 120 Crore, a prohibition on import of fully assembled drones and GST on drones reduced to a uniform 5% with effect from September 2025
- Rapid expansion of India's drone ecosystem — as on 9th February 2026, 38,575 drones had been issued Unique Identification Numbers and 244 Remote Pilot Training Organisations had been approved by the DGCA
- Commissioning of the Mahad, Raigad and Bengaluru facilities expected to expand installed capacity and strengthen the ability to serve chemical, pharmaceutical and industrial clients as well as the defence and aerospace vertical
- Growing revenue contribution expected from the defence and aerospace vertical as existing customer engagements expand
- Captive solar power initiative expected to reduce power costs, against a backdrop of rising industrial electricity tariffs
- Commodity and energy price volatility from the West Asia conflict is a key variable given the direct linkage between crude oil prices and HDPE/PP polymer costs
- Extended Producer Responsibility rules under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016 as amended are progressively pushing the industry toward recycled-content and reuse obligations
- Existing customer engagements in the defence and aerospace segment, with a growing contribution to revenue expected as these engagements expand
- A diversified pipeline spanning both product and service engagements, with sustained engagement with defence research and development organisations, the armed forces and other institutional customers on qualification and supply programmes

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Deliberate diversification from commodity plastic packaging toward higher-value, engineering-led segments — blow moulding and composite fabrication, and most recently aerospace-grade composite UAV manufacturing
- Build and scale an in-house design, manufacturing and testing capability in defence and aerospace, treating it as a natural extension of core precision-moulding and composite-fabrication capabilities
- Extend across the drone value chain from products into Drone as a Service (DAAS) through the joint venture Jyoti Aeronext Private Limited, offering infrastructure inspection, industrial monitoring, surveillance and other mission-critical services
- Expand the manufacturing footprint across Maharashtra and Karnataka through continued development at Mahad, Raigad and a new facility at Bengaluru
- Progress a captive solar power initiative to manage long-term energy costs
- Diversify away from concentration in traditional carboy/barrel product lines into pail buckets, toys, automotive components and the defence/aerospace drone vertical
- Pursue collaborations with defence and aerospace organisations to move into high-technology, higher-margin segments
- Captive solar power initiative, whose progress is expected to reduce power costs and support long-term sustainability objectives

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 was described as a year of capacity and capability expansion. The Company operates a growing manufacturing footprint across Maharashtra and Karnataka, with continued development of its facility at Mahad, Raigad and a new facility at Bengaluru strengthening its production capabilities. During the year the Company also progressed a captive solar power initiative and established an in-house design and manufacturing capability in the advanced defence and aerospace segment, extending its composite-fabrication expertise into the design, engineering and manufacture of unmanned aerial vehicles; this was further broadened through a dedicated joint venture, Jyoti Aeronext Private Limited, offering drone-enabled services for civilian and commercial applications, positioning the Company across both drone products and drone-based services. Funding capacity was strengthened by the Initial Public Offering completed during the year and the listing of equity shares on the NSE EMERGE platform on 11 August 2025, with the Board stating that the resulting increase in net worth provides a foundation to support future growth and expansion plans; no dividend was recommended so as to conserve resources for growth plans and business expansion. No commissioning dates, project cost or added capacity figures for the Mahad, Bengaluru or solar initiatives are stated in this text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Customised, client-specific moulding solutions in an industry where competition is principally on product quality, customisation capability, delivery reliability and proximity to the customer's plant
- In-house logistics, testing and labelling facilities supporting the product range
- Diversified client base of more than 1,000 customers across chemical, lubricant, pharmaceutical, paint, adhesive, food and agro, childcare, automotive and defence end-markets
- In-house design, manufacturing and testing capability in the defence and aerospace vertical, extended from established composite-fabrication and precision-moulding expertise
- Vertically integrated position spanning both drone products and drone-based services following formation of a dedicated joint venture
- More than three decades of manufacturing continuity, from the promoter partnership firm 'Jyoti Industries' in 1990 through incorporation in 2004 and NSE Emerge listing in August 2025

- Customer and segment concentration risk — A significant share of revenue remains concentrated in the traditional carboy/barrel product lines; mitigated through active diversification into pail buckets, toys, automotive components and the new defence/aerospace drone vertical.
- Execution risk in aerospace and defence — Certification, airworthiness and defence-procurement cycles are inherently long and determined by external agencies, which can influence the pace at which specific engagements translate into scaled, recurring revenue; mitigated through in-house design, manufacturing and testing capability, a diversified product-and-service pipeline and sustained engagement with defence R&D organisations, the armed forces and other institutional customers.
- Operational risk — product quality and skilled manpower — Maintaining consistent product quality in mass production and availability of skilled manpower remain ongoing operational challenges; mitigated through inventory management techniques, process controls and retention-focused HR practices.
- Competition risk and end-market demand fluctuation — The Company operates in a competitive environment exposed to demand fluctuations across packaging, infrastructure, automotive and FMCG end-markets; mitigated through product and end-market diversification.
- Industry fragmentation and supplier-side concentration in the value chain — Polymer feedstock (HDPE, PP) is supplied by a small number of large integrated petrochemical producers, while the downstream processing and moulding segment in which JGPL operates is highly fragmented and dominated by small and medium enterprises, competing principally on quality, customisation, delivery reliability and proximity to the customer's plant.
- Plastic-waste regulation and Extended Producer Responsibility obligations — EPR rules under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016 as amended are progressively pushing the industry toward recycled-content and reuse obligations, administered through the CPCB's centralised EPR portal.
- Pace of commercialisation of the new drone and aerospace vertical — The cautionary statement identifies the pace of commercialisation of the Company's new drone and aerospace vertical among the external and internal factors beyond its control that could cause actual results to differ materially from forward-looking statements.
